To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The rate for the Higgs decay to two photons is increased or decreased by a factor of up to three orders magnitude in SUSY models relative to the standard model.

the rates for the loop-induced Higgs production processes Z → Hγ, Hγγ and H-gluon gluon are increased or decreased (by as much as three orders of magnitude) in the supersymmetric model relative to the standard model.
• The Higgs bosons in SUSY theories can be produced through loop processes at LEP and SLC with rates that are orders of magnitude larger than the standard model rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for SUSY particles at LEP and SLC.

the question of how the standard model can be tested by the search for new phenomena, and how supersymmetry can be detected even if the supersymmetric particles themselves are too heavy to produce in accelerators.
the search for SUSY through the Higgs sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, even if supersymmetric particles are too heavy for direct observation, the standard model can be distinguished from minimal supersymmetry by a precise measurement of Γ(Z or Z∗ → Hγ).
a measurement of Z → γH at LEP or SLC would be the first step towards the discovery of supersymmetry.
the measurement of the Higgs width Γ( H → γγ) is the most sensitive test of the standard model and the most promising test for supersymmetric models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a Higgs boson with a mass below the Z boson is not only a necessary, but also a sufficient condition for supersymmetry.
a Higgs search at LEP or the SSC can be a SUSY search as well.
the SUSY contributions to Higgs decays can be used to probe the supersymmetric parameter space.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in a supersymmetric model, the loop-induced Higgs production processes are not suppressed by the SUSY mass scale and are enhanced by the large SUSY loop contributions, making the measurement of these processes a promising tool for the detection of supersymmetry.
a measurement of Z → γ γ at SLC or Z ∗ γ γ at LEP can distinguish the standard model from minimal supersymmetry.
a loop-induced Higgs production process is an ideal tool for searching for new physics at accelerators, and that Higgs production at SLC or at LEP is an excellent place to look.
